live_transport_p0_bank_probe.summary:
G4 live transport, FOUR runs on 2026-08-10. RUN 1 (01:5x, PID 28104): first runtime evidence, ping 18/20. RUN 2 (02:23, clean PID 20796): ping 20/20 ACK -> run-1 failures were transient Bank noise. Both runs used the host default 5.0s poll window, and both mis-attributed host-side timeouts as kernel errors. RUN 3 (03:14, PID 36916, n=100, --poll-timeout 15.0, artifacts/galaxy-vibe/p0-transport-stallproof-0210d) is the DECISIVE measurement: timeout_count=0 (was 11 at the 5s window) -> the previously suspected 'periodic saturation degradation' was an ARTEFACT of the 5s observation window truncating slow-but-healthy samples into host-side INTERNAL_ERROR. Root-cause anchor: INTERNAL_ERROR is never emitted by any kernel .galaxy source (grep is empty); it is produced solely by the Python host at vibe_host.py:1052 (poll timeout) and :1042 (step failure). Therefore any INTERNAL_ERROR observed by a probe is by definition a host-side condition, never a kernel adjudication. RUN 3 also cleared two of the three anomalies outright: illegal_requests reached adjudication_complete=true with 5/5 real kernel verdicts (UNKNOWN_OPERATION / INVALID_ARGS / COUNT_OUT_OF_RANGE / PLAYER_OUT_OF_RANGE / UNKNOWN_OPERATION), indeterminate_count=0 - the two earlier INTERNAL_ERRORs there were the same 5s truncation. RUN 3 exposed the third anomaly as a REAL KERNEL DEFECT rather than noise: with a 15s window and 3 retries the foreign-session probe still returned INTERNAL_ERROR 3/3 (foreign_session_outcome=indeterminate), which cannot be explained by stalls. Static reading of LibVibeKernel.galaxy confirmed it: the PollLoop at line ~2056 DISCARDS the return value of libVibeKernel_gf_Dispatch (responses are landed in the Bank by each handler, or by the KERNEL001_PESSIMISTIC placeholder). The session-check branch returns BEFORE that placeholder is written, so the SESSION_EXPIRED verdict was never written to the Bank at all - a SILENT REJECTION. The safety property was intact (the request never executed, state_version unchanged) but the rejection was unobservable: from the host, 'rejected' and 'kernel is dead' looked identical. FIX (VIBE-KERNEL-003): the session-reject branch now writes its SESSION_EXPIRED response to the Bank 'response' key before returning (deliberately NOT via WriteResponseToBank, so a rejected request does not pollute index/last_request_id or state_version). Kernel mirrors re-synced (sync_copies -> 3 copies byte-identical, sha a86be183, 141065 B); test_kernel 59 passed; run-all-validation 52/52; map rebuilt to C:/tmp/VibeDeadOfNight-Gen-k003.SC2Map (5,496,713 B) with all compile-time gates OK. RUN 4 (03:23, same PID 36916, k003 map) is the clean A/B control - same probe, same 15s window, only the kernel differs: foreign_session_rejected=true, foreign_session_error=SESSION_EXPIRED, foreign_attempts=1, foreign_session_outcome=rejected. Session criteria are now GREEN. REMAINING GAPS (2 of 7 verdict criteria): (A) p95 latency is a genuine, reproducible failure, not a metric artefact - two independent measurements agree closely (n=100: median 685ms / p95 4904ms / max 7201ms / 15 samples over 2s; n=20 on k003: median 693ms / p95 4776ms / max 4824ms / 3 over 2s). Already ruled out: the old latencies[int(n*0.95)] metric bug (fixed to nearest-rank, gate NOT relaxed), and monotonic Bank-growth degradation (healthy-request medians show ZERO drift across deciles: 721/671/658/687/708/677/680/690/684/715 ms). The floor is structural - the kernel PollLoop ends in Wait(0.5, c_timeGame), so ~0.5s polling plus Bank IO explains the ~690ms median; the over-2s samples cluster with a period of roughly 10-11 requests (~7s wall clock) and often in adjacent pairs, pointing at a periodic stall inside the poll loop or the engine. Not yet fully attributed - recorded honestly as an open performance defect rather than guessed at. (B) all_acked shows a single HANDLER_ABORTED per run (n=100 index 86; n=20 one sample), i.e. the known ~1% Bank lossy-channel floor, returned fast (671ms) as a real kernel verdict.

RUN4/RUN5 (VIBE-KERNEL-004, p95 root cause found and fixed). Static attribution: the VIBE-KERNEL-001 watchdog thread wrote its heartbeat via gf_WriteBankInt every 2.0s, and gf_WriteBankInt is BankSave(gv_bankHandle) - i.e. it flushed the kernel's whole in-memory state back onto the RPC bank GalaxyVibe.SC2Bank. VIBE_KERNEL_002 had already established (2026-08-08 live forensics) that any BankSave preceding the pending_request_id read permanently erases the host's request; that discipline was applied to the PollLoop thread only. The watchdog was a second, uncoordinated writer on the same bank and had never obeyed it. Quantitative prediction: danger window ~0-500ms per request vs a 2000ms watchdog period gives ~12.5% collision probability; measured over_2s was 15/100. The host's at-least-once reassert (reassert_sec=2.0 in _poll_response) recovered every erased request, which is why the defect presented as latency quantised in ~2s steps rather than as data loss - the reassert had been masking the bug, not fixing it. Fix: route the watchdog's heartbeat and restart counter to the VIBE_GEN_007 model bank (gf_WriteModelBankInt), which is already channel-isolated from the RPC bank. A/B on identical probe settings (n=100, 15s poll window), only the kernel differs: p95 4904.06ms -> 778.10ms (run4) and 1819.53ms (run5); max 7200.88 -> 2797.07 / 16459.79; over_2s 15 -> 1 / 5; median essentially unchanged 684.51 -> 686.18 / 752.44, confirming the structural Wait(0.5, c_timeGame) floor was untouched and only the pathological tail was removed. p95_within_2s is now true in 2/2 runs, but run5's margin is thin (1819/2000) and one run5 sample stalled 16.46s (~8 consecutive failed reasserts), so a smaller residual erase source remains and the criterion is NOT treated as steady-state green.
blocked_followups: residual erase source: NOT observed in run6 (all_acked=true, 0 timeouts) nor run4; only run5 (16.46s stall) ever showed it, so it is now a rare/transient candidate-bank-stale episode rather than systemic. Keep monitoring across more clean-instance runs before declaring fully closed.
decide p95<=2s steady-state: RESOLVED as steady-state green by run4 (778ms) + run6 (740ms), two independent clean runs against the lone marginal run5 (1820ms). The fix holds.

kernel_fix_2.title: watchdog must not BankSave the RPC bank (p95 tail root cause)
kernel_fix_2.symptom: bank_poll latency quantised in ~2s steps; p95 4904ms against a 2000ms budget, over_2s 15/100, while median stayed at the 684ms structural floor
kernel_fix_2.root_cause: the watchdog thread called gf_WriteBankInt('index','watchdog_last_seen_poll') every 2.0s; that is BankSave on the RPC bank, which erases a host request that landed after the PollLoop's last ReloadBank. The VIBE_KERNEL_002 read-first discipline covered the PollLoop thread only, never the watchdog.
kernel_fix_2.fix: heartbeat and kernel_restart_count now go to the model bank via gf_WriteModelBankInt (VIBE_GEN_007 channel split); RPC-bank flush still guaranteed by the VIBE_KERNEL_005 first-pass flush plus each handler's response write
kernel_fix_2.verified_by: A/B control, identical probe settings, kernel-only difference - artifacts/galaxy-vibe/p0-transport-stallproof-0210d (pre-fix p95 4904ms, over_2s 15) vs artifacts/galaxy-vibe/p0-transport-k004 (p95 778ms, over_2s 1) and artifacts/galaxy-vibe/p0-transport-k004-rep2 (p95 1820ms, over_2s 5)
kernel_fix_2.static_gates: sync_copies 3-way byte-identical sha 82c03972 / 142654B; test_kernel + test_generate_invoke_adapters 92 passed; run-all-validation 52/52; map rebuild C:/tmp/VibeDeadOfNight-Gen-k004.SC2Map (5,497,677B) all compile gates OK
kernel_fix_2.residual: run5 sample 45 stalled 16.46s and exceeded the 15s poll window (~8 consecutive failed reasserts). Working hypothesis: bank_request_landed requires the request in EVERY candidate bank file, so a diverged/stale candidate keeps the reassert loop failing; same suspected origin as the ~1% HANDLER_ABORTED floor.
